name: derbfine
sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Derbfine meant "true kin" in early Irish law. It named the closest kin group. The group held the descendants of the same great-grandfather. These kin shared land. No member could sell that land without the consent of the others. The group carried joint responsibility for wrongs. It answered for the honor price, called the éric, for injuries its members caused. The fine was often paid in cows.
objective: This entry records derbfine, the closest kin group in early Irish law.
key_results: It covered descendants of the same great-grandfather.
